reconcile.note: Henry places Mark's forty-day wilderness ordeal entirely before John's 'next day' scene, reading it as Jesus's return from the desert, not the day after his baptism.

discrepancy.note: Strauss argues the Synoptics' forty-day wilderness sojourn leaves no room in John's tight day-by-day sequence from baptism to Cana.

quotes.text: But there is, besides, a chronological difficulty: namely, that while, according to the synoptical writers, Jesus…for forty days to the wilderness, where the temptation occurs, and then returns into Galilee; John, on the contrary, is silent concerning the temptation, and appears to suppose an interval of a few days only, between the baptism of Jesus and his journey into Galilee;
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §53, on Mark 1:12 and John 1:35.
